list.item:
Political and military situation in China:
I. Anti-American demonstrations; Communist rejection of Government proposals for resumption of negotiations; Communist military offensives in Manchuria (January–February)
II. Resignation of T.V. Soong; expulsion of Communist liaison delegations from Government-held areas; meetings of the Central Executive Committee of the Kuomintang (March 1–April 17)
III. Reorganization of the Government (April 18–May 16)
IV. Anti-Government student demonstrations; meetings of the People’s Political Council; critical position of Government forces in Manchuria (May 19–July 3)
V. Government mobilization to suppress Communist rebellion; changes in the command of Government forces in Manchuria; appointment of T.V. Soong as Governor of Kwangtung Province; fourth plenary session of the Central Executive Committee of the Kuomintang (July 4–October 2)
VI. Renewed Communist offensive in Manchuria; Government’s measures against the Democratic League; critical postion of Government forces (October 2–December 31)

item.ref: Reports on the situation in Formosa (Taiwan), particularly respecting Formosan dissatisfaction with administrative policies of the Chinese Government
Representations by the United States regarding the status of the port of Dairen; failure of Sino-Soviet negotiations to allow occupation of Dairen by Chinese Government
Unsuccessful attempts to resolve political problems in Sinkiang; extent of Soviet aid and encouragement to rebel groups in Sinkiang; border incident at Peitashan
Status of Tibet; Tibetan trade mission

Council of Foreign Ministers meeting at Moscow: United States opposition to placing China question on agenda; exchange of views between the United States and the Soviet Union regarding withdrawal of troops from China
Consideration of withdrawal of American consular officers from cities in in danger of Communist occupation
Mission to China of Lieutenant General Albert C. Wedemeyer to appraise the political, economic, psychological, and military situation
Military aid to China: Chinese requests for ammunition and military matériel and equipment; lifting of embargo on arms shipments to China; attempts to speed flow of supplies to China

United States naval aid to China: Continued withdrawal of United States Marines and turnover of abandoned ammunition to Chinese Government; incidents affecting American personnel; negotiations of agreement for transfer of naval vessels to China
Problems respecting repatriation of Japanese still remaining in China, particularly in Manchuria
Discussions regarding proposed Sino-American cooperative mapping agreement
Exchange of notes terminating the Sino-American special technical cooperative agreement of April 15, 1943
Request by the Chinese Government for an American adviser on civil aeronautics
Negotiations between the United States and China respecting joint effort in the exploration of China for minerals of importance in the atomic energy programs of the two governments

Financial relations between the United States and China: Chinese requests for financial assistance; representations regarding fixing of an equitable rate of exchange for expenditures by American armed forces and diplomatic establishment in China; interest of the United States in Chinese measures to protect its economy from a violently inflationary situation
Problems arising in the implementation of the surplus property agreement of August 30, 1946
Agreement between the United States and China respecting the United States Educational Foundation in China, signed at Nanking, November 10, 1947
Agreement between the United States and China regarding relief assistance to China, signed October 27, 1947
Representations regarding impact of Chinese tax laws and regulations on American consular property
Representations by the embassy in China regarding discriminatory provisions of Chinese income tax law and regulations
Interest of the United States in conditions for American participation in economic development of China
Representations regarding the reregistration of American real property rights in China
Problems with respect to liquidation of assets in the former International Settlement at Shanghai and the Diplomatic Quarter at Peiping
Request of Chinese Government for revision of the Sino-American air transport agreement of December 20, 1946

Establishment of an executive office in the embassy in China to enable the ambassador to exercise over-all supervision and coordination of basic policies governing official American activities in China
Representations regarding release of Major Robert B. Rigg and Captain John W. Collins, assistant military attachés in China, captured by Chinese Communist armed forces in Manchuria
